entry.title: Device Bound Session Credentials in ASP.NET Core
entry.summary: A session cookie is a bearer token, which is a polite way of saying that whoever holds it is you. Copy the cookie, replay it from another machine, and the server happily serves your account. Nothing about the request proves which device it came from, so a cookie lifted by malware, an XSS payload, or a stray database backup keeps working until it expires. For a long-lived session, that can be weeks.
